subject.title: fix(mcp): honor `disabled` flag to prevent spawning disabled servers

question: Should `mcp.servers.*.disabled` become a permanent public alias, or should OpenClaw keep `enabled` canonical and handle this foreign spelling only through validation, import, or doctor migration?
rationale: The branch changes a user-facing config contract and steady-state runtime behavior, so implementation cannot safely settle the permanent alias policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep one canonical key
options.body: Retain `enabled` as the only runtime setting and reject or explicitly migrate `disabled` outside steady-state reads.

options.title: Approve the alias contract
options.body: Support `disabled` publicly after defining canonical precedence, writeback, migration, documentation, and fresh-install and upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep one canonical key
recommendation.body: Retain `enabled` as the only runtime setting and reject or explicitly migrate `disabled` outside steady-state reads.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing MCP alias and canonicalization pattern appears most directly connected to this product-contract decision.
